case_title: State of Rajasthan v. Leela Ram @ Leela Dhar
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.27
aggravating_circumstances: Use of a sharp-edged weapon on a vital part of the body, resulting in death
high_court_outcome: Modified conviction to s.304 Part II
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was that three persons, including the respondent, attacked the victim and caused serious injuries to him. The respondent inflicted an axe injury on the skull of the deceased, which caused his death. The trial court convicted the respondent based on the depositions of four eye-witnesses, medical evidence, and the recovery of a blood-stained axe. The High Court modified the conviction to an offence under s.304 Part II, but the Supreme Court restored the trial court's conviction under s.302 IPC. The evidence indicated that the respondent wielded the axe, which caused the fatal injury to the victim's skull, leading to his death. The medical report confirmed that the injury was severe and resulted in the victim's death.
